_meta.what_this_is: Four claimed effects an analyst might report, each carrying the raw signal all three guards read: the aggregate effect and its per-segment effects (for the Simpson/confounder guard), the treated change and a same-way-selected control's change (for the regression-to-the-mean guard), and a p-value plus the number of tests that were run to find it (for the multiple-comparisons guard). A real effect is consistent across segments, beats its control, and clears the Bonferroni threshold alpha/n_tests.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. Each finding is hand-authored so exactly one guard is the one that catches it, and the 'real' flag is the ground truth used to score false and true discoveries. coaching is a regression-to-the-mean artifact (its control moved as much); new_model is a Simpson reversal (positive aggregate, negative in every segment); metric_7 is a multiple-comparisons fluke (raw p 0.03 but 1 of 20 tests); real_fix is a genuine effect that passes all three.
_meta.format: findings [{id, claim, aggregate_effect, segments[], treated_change, control_change, p_value, n_tests, real}]. alpha is 0.05, set in the script.

findings.claim: coaching raised the bottom cohort's score by 8.5 points
the new model beats the old by 5 points overall
the retrieval fix raised answer accuracy by 6 points
